name: Rabi' al-Thani
intro: Days 1, 3, 6, 8, 10, 12, 13, 22, 25, 29 and 30 of the month of Rabi' al-Thani carry memorable events of Shi'a history. The martyrdom of Lady Zahra (PBUH) and Imam al-Baqir (PBUH), according to one account the passing of Lady Ma'suma (PBUH), and the death of Musa Mubarqa' are among the sorrowful events of this month. The birth of Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH), his journey to Jurjan, the uprising of Mukhtar and of the Tawwabin, the death of Khalid ibn al-Walid, and the fall of the Umayyads are among the joyful events this month has witnessed.

events.title: The Uprising of the Tawwabin
events.text:
On this day in the year 65 AH, Sulayman ibn Surad, together with a group of the Tawwabin (the Penitents) — sixteen thousand of whom had been registered in Sulayman's ledger — rose up to avenge Imam Husayn (PBUT).
On the second of Rabi' al-Thani they set out from Nukhayla in Kufa to fight the accursed Ibn Ziyad. On the night of Friday, the 5th of Rabi' al-Thani, they left Kufa, and the next day they went to the grave of Hazrat Aba Abdillah (PBUH). They stayed in Karbala for one or three days and nights, weeping, seeking forgiveness, and wailing and lamenting, so much so that the sound of such wailing had never been heard in that valley, before or since.
At the time of farewell, the area around the Imam's grave was as crowded as the crowd around the Ka'ba. Each person recited poetry and lamented in his own way and bade farewell to the Imam, preparing himself to fight Ibn Ziyad.
Sulayman was one of the Shi'a of Ali ibn Abi Talib and of Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (PBUT), and he had been present in all the battles at the side of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH). In the end they met the army of Ibn Ziyad, and after killing a great number of them and after many struggles and acts of self-sacrifice, Sulayman was martyred at Ayn al-Warda at the age of 93. Of Sulayman's companions only 27 — wounded, exhausted and thirsty — survived; all the rest were martyred.
The accursed Husayn ibn Numayr — who had burned the hearts of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) in Karbala — was killed at Ayn al-Warda at the hands of Ibrahim, son of Malik al-Ashtar, and went to Hell.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 4, p. 68.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 45, p. 359.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 168.
Those seeking the details of this episode should refer to the books Rawdat al-Safa, Nasikh al-Tawarikh, and Qala'id al-Nuhur, Rabi' al-Thani volume.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 191.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam al-Baqir (PBUH)
events.text: According to one narration, this day is the day of the martyrdom of Imam al-Baqir (PBUH).
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 177.

events.title: Imam al-Askari's (PBUH) Journey to Jurjan
events.text:
On this day Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH), in order to fulfill a promise he had made — and as one of his miracles was revealed — traveled from Samarra to Jurjan without the need to traverse the distance (tayy al-ard).
Ja'far ibn Sharif says: One year I intended to go on Hajj, and before the Hajj I went to visit Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH) in Samarra. I had with me funds belonging to the Shi'a that I was to deliver to the Imam. I wanted to ask him to whom I should give the funds, but before I spoke, the Imam said: “Give it to Mubarak the servant.” I said: I have already done so. Then I left and said: “Your Shi'a in Jurjan send you their greetings.” The Imam (PBUH) said: Aren't you returning to Jurjan after the Hajj rituals? I said: I am.
He said: In 170 days, at the beginning of Friday, the third of Rabi' al-Thani, you will enter Jurjan. Then announce to the people that I will come to Jurjan at the end of that same day. Go in safety.
Almighty God will bring you and what is with you safely to your family and children. A son has been born for you. Name him “Salt”, for God will soon bring him to perfection, and he will be one of our friends.
I said: O son of the Messenger of God, Ibrahim ibn Isma'il al-Jurjani is one of your Shi'a, and every year he gives more than a hundred thousand dirhams in charity to your friends, and he is among those in Jurjan who enjoy the blessings of God. The Imam (PBUH) said: “May God reward Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Isma'il with good for the charity he gives to our Shi'a, forgive his sins, and grant him a son, sound of limb, who will uphold the truth. Tell Ibrahim: Hasan ibn Ali says: Name your son Ahmad.”
The narrator says: I took leave of the Imam, went on Hajj and returned, and on the day the Imam had appointed I arrived safely in Jurjan. When our companions came to congratulate me, I told them: The Imam (PBUH) has promised me that he will come here at the end of today. So get ready, and prepare your questions and needs.
After performing the noon and afternoon prayers, the Shi'a gathered at my house. Suddenly Imam al-Askari (PBUH) entered at the very hour he had said. Upon entering he greeted us, and we hurried to welcome him and kissed his hand. Then the Imam said: I had promised Ja'far ibn Sharif that I would come to you at the end of this day. I performed the noon and afternoon prayers in Samarra and came to you to renew my covenant with you. Now bring your needs and questions.
The first person to ask was Nadr ibn Jabir. He said: O son of the Messenger of God, my son is blind in both eyes; pray that God restore his sight. The Imam said: Bring him. He brought him, and the Imam passed his blessed hand over his eyes, and his eyes were restored to sight.
After him, they came one by one and stated their needs, and the Imam fulfilled their needs until everyone's needs were met and their questions answered, and on the same day he returned to Samarra.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 50, p. 263.

events.title: Death of Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik
events.text:
On Wednesday, the 6th of Rabi' al-Thani in the year 125 AH, Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik died in Rusafa and went to Hell.
He was a cross-eyed, coarse, ill-tempered and miserly man, greedy for amassing wealth. He ordered the killing of Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (PBUT), summoned Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq (PBUT) to Syria, subjected them to many insults, and in the end had Imam al-Baqir (PBUH) martyred. He ruled as caliph for 19 years, 9 months and ten days, and hurried to Hell at the age of 53.
In the time of al-Saffah, when the killing of the Umayyads had begun and their graves were being dug up and whatever was found was burned, when it came to the grave of al-Walid, no trace remained in it, and of Abd al-Malik part of his skull was left. When Hisham's grave was opened, his body had still not decomposed, so they struck it with eighty lashes, burned it, and scattered its ashes to the wind.
Some have said that the eighty lashes given to Hisham were apparently the punishment (hadd) for slander (qadhf), since he had insulted the mother of Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (PBUT).
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 128.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 118 - 127. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 191. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 228.

events.title: Birth of Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 232 AH, Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH) illuminated the world with his arrival. According to the narration of Misbah, Taqwim al-Muhsinin, Ikhtiyarat and Durus of the Shahid, the Imam's birth was on the fourth of this month. Other views on his birth also exist, which are the 27th of Dhu al-Hijja and the 10th of Rabi' al-Thani.
His father was Imam al-Hadi (PBUH) and his honored mother was a lady whose name is Hadith, Hadithah, Susan or Salil. His birthplace was Medina, his most famous titles are Zaki and Naqi, and his kunya is Abu Muhammad.
In order to keep him under watch and monitor his comings and goings, the Abbasid court had housed him in the residential quarter of the Turkish-descended soldiers; and it is from this that he is called “al-Askari” (the military one).
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 132. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 229.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 185.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 23.
Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 10. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 30.
Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, p. 24. Irshad: vol. 2, p. 313.
Tatimmat al-Mukhtasar fi Akhbar al-Bashar: vol. 1, p. 348.

events.title: Martyrdom of Lady Siddiqa Tahira (PBUH)
events.text: According to a narration that holds the fortieth day after the passing of the Prophet (SAWW) to be the day of the martyrdom of Lady Zahra (PBUH), the 8th of Rabi' al-Thani is counted as the day of her martyrdom.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: Rabi' al-Awwal and Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 204.

events.title: Passing of Lady Ma'suma (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 201 AH, according to the well-known view, is the anniversary of the martyrdom-like passing of Lady Fatima Ma'suma (PBUH) — the beloved of God, the lady of the world's creation, the devout, ascetic, perfect and chaste — daughter of Imam Musa al-Kazim (PBUH).
Seventeen days after entering the city of Qom, with a broken and grieving heart from the loss of her father and separation from her brother, she passed away. Qom was wholly enveloped in sorrow and mourning for her. Her pure body was washed and shrouded, and brought to the garden of Musa ibn Khazraj — the present site of the holy shrine. Two veiled horsemen came from outside the city and prayed over her body. Then they entered the vault, buried the pure body, and left, and no one recognized them.
Musa ibn Khazraj endowed that garden as a waqf for Lady Ma'suma (PBUH), and placed a roof of reed and matting over her blessed grave. This structure remained until Zaynab, daughter of Imam al-Jawad (PBUH), built a dome over the noble grave. Later a number of daughters of the Imams (PBUT) were buried there. When Umm Muhammad, daughter of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida (PBUH), died, she was buried beside her. After that, Maymuna, the sister of Umm Muhammad, passed away, and she too was buried next to Umm Muhammad. Another dome was built over these two graves, so that two adjoining domes stood over the graves of Lady Fatima Ma'suma (PBUH), Umm Muhammad and Maymuna.
Besides the daughters of the Infallibles (PBUT), two maidservants are also buried there. During the renovation of the floor of the holy shrine in the time of Naser al-Din Shah, an opening to a vault was discovered and several righteous women entered the vault. They saw the pure body of Maymuna and of two of the maidservants still fresh after a thousand years. This vault is located next to the vault of Lady Fatima Ma'suma (PBUH).
The late Namazi reports the passing of Lady Ma'suma (PBUH) on the 12th of Rabi' al-Thani in the year 201 AH, and the view attributed to Shaykh Hurr al-Amili (RA) is the 8th of Sha'ban in the year 201 AH.
Imam al-Sadiq (PBUH) said: “Qom is a little Kufa, and Paradise has eight gates, three of which belong to Qom. In that city a woman from my descendants will pass away, whose name is Fatima, and she is the daughter of Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH); through her intercession all my Shi'a will enter Paradise.”
sources: Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 163. Muntakhab-e Daryay-e Sokhan: p. 34. Zendegani-ye Karima-ye Ahl al-Bayt (PBUH): p. 83.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 60, pp. 219 - 220. Ajsad-e Javidan: p. 105.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 8, p. 257.
Hayat al-Sunnat: p. 11.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 57, p. 228.

events.title: The Fall of the Umayyads
events.text: On this day allegiance was pledged to al-Saffah, the first Abbasid caliph, and with the extinction of the Marwanid state, the Umayyad state came to a complete end. Of course Marwan was killed on the 27th of Dhu al-Hijja, but on this day, with the founding of the Abbasid state, the name of the Umayyads was officially erased from the page of the caliphate.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 95, p. 357.

events.title: Martyrdom of Lady Zahra (PBUH)
events.text: According to the narration of the late Ibn Shahr Ashub in Manaqib, and of al-Qaramani in Akhbar al-Duwal, the martyrdom of Umm Abiha, Fatima al-Zahra (PBUH), took place on this day.
sources: Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 3, p. 406. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 219.

events.title: The Uprising of Mukhtar
events.text:
On this day Mukhtar — the one who gladdened the broken hearts of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) — rose up in Kufa with the cry of “Ya li-Tharat al-Husayn” (O avengers of Husayn). Mukhtar was born in Ta'if in the first year of the Hijra and was martyred in Kufa in the year 67 AH at the hands of Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr. His kunya is Abu Ishaq. His father, Abu Ubayda, was a great companion who was martyred in the war against the Persians. After the father, his two brothers Hakam and Jubayr were martyred.
In the eighteen months of his rule, Mukhtar sent eighteen thousand of the killers of the Master of Martyrs (PBUH) to Hell. This is apart from those who were killed by his companions and followers and by Ibrahim ibn Malik al-Ashtar outside Kufa and beside the Khazir River.
Sa'd, Mukhtar's uncle, was governor of Mada'in on behalf of the Commander of the Faithful and Imam Hasan (PBUT), and whenever he went somewhere he left Mukhtar in his place.
The Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) informed him of victory and triumph, and Maytham al-Tammar gave him the good news in the prison of Kufa.
On the day of Eid al-Adha, Abu Muhammad Hakam ibn Mukhtar came to Imam al-Baqir (PBUH). After introducing himself, Imam al-Baqir (PBUH) called him close, and he said: My master, people say many things about my father. By God, the truth is your word, and whatever you say I accept. The Imam (PBUH) said: Glory be to God. My father informed me that my mother's dowry came from money that Mukhtar sent to my father. Mukhtar rebuilt our ruined homes, killed our enemies, and avenged every drop of blood that was shed from us. Then he said three times: May God have mercy on your father.
In childhood, the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) would seat him on his knee and show him kindness and favor. Imam al-Baqir (PBUH) said: By God, my father informed me that Mukhtar used to come to Fatima, daughter of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), and that lady would spread a mat for him and place a cushion for him. Then he said: “Every right we had with anyone, he demanded it.”
In another narration he said: “When Mukhtar sent the foul head of Ubaydullah to Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH), the Imam was at the table; he rejoiced and prayed.”
According to another view, the uprising of Mukhtar was on the night of the 14th of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 66 AH; and according to another, on the 16th of Rabi' al-Thani.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, pp. 225 - 229. Fursan al-Hayja': vol. 2, p. 217. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 45, p. 333. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 4, p. 68. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: Rabi' al-Awwal and Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 226.
Fursan al-Hayja': vol. 2, pp. 198, 199, 244, 245.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 45, p. 386.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 45, p. 333. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 232.

events.title: Death of Musa Mubarqa'
events.text:
Musa Mubarqa' (PBUH), son of Imam al-Jawad (PBUH), passed away in the city of Qom in the year 296 AH. According to one account, his death was on the 8th of Rabi' al-Thani.
According to another view, the death of Musa Mubarqa' occurred on the 14th of Rabi' al-Thani. His grave is well known in Chehel Akhtaran in Qom, on Azar Street.
Name: Musa; kunya: Abu Ja'far; title: Mubarqa', because out of excessive beauty he covered his blessed face with a veil. Father: Jawad al-A'imma (PBUH); his mother was a maidservant.
He was among the first of the Radawi Sayyids to enter Qom, in the year 256 AH. He always wore a veil over his face, but the Arab inhabitants of Qom expelled him from Qom, and he went to Kashan, where he was shown respect.
After Abu al-Sadim Husayn ibn Ali ibn Adam and another of the leaders of Qom came, the Arabs of Qom realized who Musa was, and brought him back to Qom and prepared a house for him. They also bought land and gardens for him in a number of villages, and his sisters Zaynab, Umm Muhammad and Maymuna, daughters of Imam al-Jawad (PBUH), came to Qom and joined him.
When Musa Mubarqa' died in Qom, the governor of Qom, Abbas ibn Amr al-Ghanawi, performed the funeral prayer over him, and he was buried at his present well-known location in Qom, which was formerly the house of Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Abi Khalid al-Ash'ari, known as Shanbula.
Kulayni (RA), in al-Kafi, with a reliable chain of transmission, reported that Musa Mubarqa' held the custodianship of the endowments (awqaf) on behalf of the Imam (PBUH).
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 50, pp. 161 - 162. Tarikh Samarra': vol. 3, p. 302.
Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 230.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 226. Mir'at al-'Uqul: vol. 6, p. 128.
al-Kafi: vol. 1, p. 261.

events.title: Mu'awiya ibn Yazid's Self-Abdication of the Caliphate
events.text:
When Yazid ibn Mu'awiya hurried to the depths of Hellfire on the 14th of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 64 AH, his son Mu'awiya took his place. After forty days, on the 25th of Rabi' al-Thani, he ascended the pulpit and delivered a sermon, recalled the deeds of his forefathers, cursed his grandfather and father, disavowed their actions, wept bitterly, and then abdicated the caliphate himself.
Marwan ibn al-Hakam, may God's curse be upon him, rose from the foot of the pulpit and said: Now that you do not seek the caliphate, then cast the matter of the caliphate aside. Mu'awiya ibn Yazid said: I have not tasted the sweetness of the caliphate, so how can I be content to taste its burdens? In any case he sat at home and busied himself with weeping, and 25 or 40 days after this event he died; according to one account he was poisoned. After him the caliphate of the descendants of Abu Sufyan came to an end and passed to Marwan and his family.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 73. Qala'id al-Nuhur: Rabi' al-Thani volume, p. 262. Tawdih al-Maqasid: pp. 12 - 13. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 255.

events.title: Death of Khalid ibn al-Walid
events.text:
On the last day of Rabi' al-Thani, Khalid ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi hurried to the lowest depths of Hell. In the later years of the Prophet's (SAWW) life, 20 years after the Prophet's mission began, he outwardly accepted Islam together with Amr ibn al-As. Abu Bakr made him governor of Syria, and Umar dismissed him. After a time he died in the city of Homs and was buried there.
On several occasions the Prophet (SAWW) disavowed Khalid's actions. Without the Prophet's (SAWW) permission he killed the Banu Jadhima, took a number of them captive, and said: “Let everyone who holds a captive kill him.” The Muhajirun and Ansar sent the captives to the Prophet (SAWW), and he raised his blessed hands and said twice: “O God, I declare to You my disavowal of what Khalid has done.” Khalid insulted Ammar. The Prophet (SAWW) said: “Whoever reviles Ammar, God will revile him.”
At Abu Bakr's command he sought to have the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) martyred, but before he could take any action the Imam became aware of it, and pressed Khalid's throat with two fingers so hard that Khalid cried out, the people fled, and Khalid soiled his clothes. Then he said: Abu Bakr and Umar commanded me to do this. Whenever anyone intervened, the Imam did not release him, until Abu Bakr sent Umar and brought Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas adjured the Imam by the pure grave of the Prophet (SAWW), by his children, and by Lady Siddiqa (PBUT), and the Imam released him. Abu Bakr said to Umar: “This is the result of consulting with you!” — since it was Umar who had chosen Khalid for this task.
Khalid ibn al-Walid also killed Malik ibn Nuwayra (RA) together with many of his tribe on the charge of not pledging allegiance to Abu Bakr, and that very night committed a transgression with Malik's wife. When Umar heard of this, he said: “I will stone you,” but he did not do it?!
In another instance, when Abu Bakr sent him against the tribe of Banu Sulaym, he gathered a group of the men of the tribe in one place and burned them in fire.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 91.
Usd al-Ghaba: vol. 2, p. 96.
Sab'a min al-Salaf: pp. 337 - 341. Sahih al-Bukhari: vol. 5, p. 107. Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba: vol. 2, p. 94.
Sab'a min al-Salaf: pp. 342 - 345.
Sharh Nahj al-Balagha by Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 13, pp. 302 - 303.
Sab'a min al-Salaf: pp. 346 - 348. Sharh of Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 1, p. 179.
Sab'a min al-Salaf: p. 347. From al-Tabaqat al-Kubra.

honorifics.(SAWW): Sallallahu Alayhi wa Alihi wa Sallam — peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny (the Prophet Muhammad)
honorifics.(PBUH): Peace Be Upon Him (used for Imams, Prophets and other holy figures, male)
honorifics.(SA): Salamullah Alayha — peace be upon her (Lady Fatima, Lady Umm Kulthum, Lady Zaynab, Lady Narjis, etc.)
honorifics.(PBUT): Peace Be Upon Them (plural, e.g. the Ahl al-Bayt / the Infallible Imams)
honorifics.(ATFS): Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu ash-Sharif — may Allah hasten his noble reappearance (the Imam of the Age)
honorifics.(RA): Rahimahullah — may Allah have mercy on him
